To determine whether a 5,000-employee self-insured employer should cover GLP-1 medications for obesity beyond type 2 diabetes, and under what utilization-management criteria, it is essential to balance clinical benefits, legal requirements, and financial implications:

GLP-1 receptor agonists like semaglutide and tirzepatide have demonstrated significant efficacy in promoting weight loss and improving metabolic parameters. The high cost of GLP-1 medications (~$1,350/month for Wegovy) poses significant financial risks to self-insured plans. Self-insured employers have the discretion to provide health insurance coverage for various medical conditions, including obesity and type 2 diabetes. Statutory Framework

In the United States, the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) governs self-insured employer health plans. The Affordable Care Act (ACA), also known as Obamacare, expanded coverage to include pre-existing conditions such as diabetes. Self-insured employers may have contractual obligations with their employees regarding health insurance coverage.
